site_or_subject: Data centre share of metered electricity consumption, 2025
record: CSO release 'Data Centres Metered Electricity Consumption 2025' (7 July 2026): data centres used 23% of Ireland's metered electricity in 2025, up from 22% in 2024 and 5% in 2015; urban households 18% and rural households 9%. The release's key findings give 7,663 GWh in 2025 vs 6,973 GWh in 2024 (+10%) and 1,991 GWh in Q4 2025 alone.

gap: none documented; the 23% figure is an official metered share.

site_or_subject: CRU Large Energy Users Connection Policy Decision CRU/2025236
operator: Commission for Regulation of Utilities (regulator); applies to all new data-centre connections
record: CRU decision CRU/2025236 (12 Dec 2025) [as summarised by Matheson LLP; the CRU's own text was not located]: new data centres >=10 MVA must provide dispatchable on-site or proximate generation/storage at least equal to their Maximum Import Capacity (de-rated), separately metered and participating in wholesale and capacity markets, before ramping to full MIC; 1-<10 MVA sites need behind-the-meter autoproduction covering 100% of MIC; all >=1 MVA sites must source >=80% of annual demand from additional Irish renewables over a 6-year glide path. 'Islanded' data centres are stated to be not in line with national policy. System Operators must submit initial proposals for publishing locational capacity and constraint maps to the CRU by 31 Mar 2026.

Matheson LLP's PDF, read 2026-10-24, is the firm's own summary of CRU/2025236, not a copy of the decision; the CRU's text was not located by search. The summary gives the 10 MVA dispatchable tier, 100% of MIC (de-rated) as behind-the-meter autoproduction for 1 to <10 MVA sites, the 80% additional-renewables requirement from 1 MVA on a 6-year glide path, the 'islanded' statement, and 31 March 2026 as the date for submitting map proposals to the CRU (corrected from 'publish ... maps'). Figures carry basis press_report until the CRU text is read.

site_or_subject: Vantage DUB 13 data centre, Profile Park (An Bord Pleanala ABP-317446-23)
record: An Bord Pleanala refused permission (4 April 2025) for a 12,893 sq m data centre (DUB 13) with 13 emergency back-up generators, departing from the Inspector's recommendation to grant. Reasons: no fixed grid connection agreement was demonstrated; the Board could not be satisfied that 'the permitted on-site gas powered generation' would not be used as the primary energy source, which would conflict with the 2022 Government Statement on Data Centres ('islanded' developments not in line with national policy) and Climate Action Plan 2024; the EIAR did not assess the no-grid-connection scenario. South Dublin County Council had refused on 29 May 2023.

site_or_subject: Amsterdam data centre siting policy 2020-2030, first revision (growth allowance withdrawn)
record: The 2020 policy capped connected-capacity growth at 67 MW per year (670 MVA by 2030). The first revision (preparatory decision 8 Nov 2023, draft 28 Dec 2023) removes the growth allowance so no further growth is currently possible under the policy. 2024 contracted data-centre capacity in Amsterdam is about 150 MW with recorded peak about 100 MW. Residual-heat use is mandatory; groundwater extraction is prohibited; data-centre drinking-water use is about 1-1.5% of supply and Waternet expects to stay below 5%.

site_or_subject: Meta hyperscale campus Zeewolde (cancelled) and national hyperscale siting rule
record: [older: 2022] On 10 June 2022 the cabinet approved a draft decree (in force 1 January 2024, Stb. 2023, 492, per the Middenmeer receipt) barring municipalities from permitting new hyperscale data centres except in two areas: the former Eemsmond part of Het Hogeland and the Agriport A7/B1 sites in Hollands Kroon; the draft decree (2023 text, Barro art. 2.15.1) defines hyperscale as more than 10 ha and 70 MW or more, and exempts applications made on or before the 16 Feb 2022 voorbereidingsbesluit. The cabinet said the rule did not apply to Zeewolde, where the zoning plan had already been adopted, but that the Rijksvastgoedbedrijf could not sell the state land to the municipality, citing a TNO assessment that some conditions were not met. The Eerste Kamer had adopted a motion on 21 Dec 2021 (35925 XIV, H) asking the government to have the Rijksvastgoedbedrijf suspend sales of agricultural land for hyperscale data centres.

site_or_subject: Microsoft Middenmeer (Agriport) drinking-water use and AMS13/14 permit
record: The Tweede Kamer adopted a motion on 4 Oct 2022 (Kamerstuk 26 643, nr. 919) recording that Microsoft's Wieringermeer data centre used 84 million litres of drinking water for cooling in 2021 against Microsoft's earlier estimate of 12 to 20 million litres, and asking the government to consider a ban or at least a cap on drinking-water use as a permit requirement for hyperscale data centres. The municipal permit documents retrieved (2020 Nota van zienswijzen for AMS13/14) contain no drinking-water volume. The province's data-centre strategy 2025-2027 records that PWN now gives drinking-water connections only for office use. No PWN or municipal meter reading for the site was found yet.

site_or_subject: Fortum heat-pump plants recovering Microsoft data-centre waste heat into district heating
record: The Ministry of Economic Affairs and Employment granted Fortum Power and Heat Oy EUR 8,234,000 of investment aid for replacing coal (release of 2 Jul 2021) to recover heat from data centres in Kirkkonummi and Espoo, the first phase being heat-pump plants of approximately 60 MW in total using waste heat; the release does not name the data-centre operator. No permit or district-heat statistic covering the Kolabacken and Hepokorpi plants' operation was located.

claim: At the March 2022 announcement, the City of Espoo, Fortum and Microsoft stated the data centres' waste heat would cover about 40% of the heat demand of 250,000 district-heat users in Espoo, Kauniainen and Kirkkonummi and cut district-heat CO2 by about 400,000 t/yr; Fortum in May 2026 restated 'approximately 40 per cent' of the area's ~2 TWh/yr demand once fully implemented. Fortum's press release (6 May 2026) states that heat production started at Kolabacken and Hepokorpi and that waste-heat recovery from the data centres starts in phases in 2027, and gives 72 water-to-water heat pumps providing up to 180 MW of district heat, 40 air-to-water heat pumps, 200 MW of electric boilers, 20,000 m3 / 800 MWh thermal storage; about EUR 225 million investment with NextGenerationEU and Finnish state support; about 250,000 heat users. The ministry's annex describing the 2021 grant says the data-centre heat project is part of a larger whole expected to cut coal use at Espoo's Suomenoja combined heat and power plant by over 600 gigawatt-hours a year.

site_or_subject: Energy Efficiency Act (EnEfG) data-centre PUE, heat-reuse and renewable obligations
record: EnEfG § 11 (statute text): data centres commissioned from 1 July 2026 must reach an energy usage effectiveness (PUE) <= 1.2 within two years of commissioning and a share of reused energy of at least 10% (planned 15% from 1 July 2027 and 20% from 1 July 2028; DIN EN 50600-4-6, with listed exemptions); existing data centres must reach PUE <= 1.5 from 1 July 2027 and <= 1.3 from 1 July 2030; electricity use must be covered on a balance-sheet basis by renewable electricity at 50% from 1 Jan 2024 and 100% from 1 Jan 2027; operators must also report to the Energieeffizienzregister fuer Rechenzentren (per the TUV summary). A government bill amending the EnEfG was still in draft when the Bundesrat gave its opinion on 10 July 2026 (BR-Drs. 388/26). Mainova (30 June 2026) reports Frankfurt's daily peak load exceeded 900 MW on 25-26 June 2026, up from clearly above 850 MW a year earlier, with grid capacity expected to more than double; the release does not attribute the load to data centres.

region: Aragon (Huesca and Zaragoza provinces: Huesca/Walqa, Villanueva de Gállego, El Burgo de Ebro, Zaragoza-La Cartuja; Calatorao)
site_or_subject: Aragon regional-interest approvals: Amazon's five site areas and Blackstone Calatorao
record: Orden FOM/1040/2025 (BOA nº 163, 25 Aug 2025) publishes the Aragon government's agreement of 22 Aug 2025 giving partial definitive approval to Amazon Data Services Spain's PIGA covering five site areas: Villanueva de Gállego 1 and 2, Huesca (Walqa 2), El Burgo de Ebro (Espartal III) and Zaragoza-La Cartuja (Acampo del Marqués, about 143 ha). The order states no MW, GWh or water volumes, sets no energy or water limits, and says the PIGA procedure continues pending INAGA procedures. Orden VFL/654/2026 (BOA nº 85, 7 May 2026) approved phase-1 building projects at Villanueva de Gállego 1 and 2 and Walqa plus two 132/20 kV substations, excluded El Burgo de Ebro's phase 1 for unmet environmental requirements, and records diesel back-up thermal input of 342 MWt (Walqa), 327 MWt (VDG1) and 1,169 MWt (VDG2). INAGA's 6 Oct 2025 declaration for Walqa's water supply covers a 9 km raw-water pipeline from the Valdabra reservoir and three proposed wells with the hydrogeological study pending, and gives no annual volume. elDiario.es (28 Aug 2025) gives over 2,000 MW and nearly 16,000 GWh/yr for the five largest projects (AWS plus Blackstone Calatorao, whose initial approval was published the same day), about 10,000 GWh consumed by all of Aragon in 2024, and about 1 million m3/yr of water for the projects [press, source not named: elDiario.es]; it reports that ten Aragon nodes on Red Eléctrica's list total 2,380 MW [press: elDiario.es]. Merca2 (16 Jul 2026) reports INAGA approval for the La Cartuja centre with an industrial-water cap of 204,697 m3/yr, about 3,280 GWh/yr and back-up generation above 1,373 MW thermal [press: Merca2].

region: EU-27 (21 member states reported per the July 2025 technical report)
site_or_subject: Energy Efficiency Directive data-centre reporting database: first technical assessment
record: The Commission's first technical report (EY, Borderstep and AIT for DG ENER, July 2025) on the 2024 reporting period under Delegated Regulation (EU) 2024/1364 covers 770 reporting data centres, about 36% of estimated EU data centres; six member states had no reported data and five had fewer than three. Germany reported the most sites (335 of an estimated 456), followed by France (133) and the Netherlands (85); Czechia reported none of an estimated 50 and Ireland 18 of an estimated 123 (15%). The report gives per-site means rather than EU totals: renewable energy about 16.8 GWh; guarantees of origin about 12.5 GWh, PPAs about 5.3 GWh (median 0; the report flags a possible unit misinterpretation) and on-site generation about 0.04 GWh. The three component means are taken over different subsets of sites and sum to about 17.8 GWh, more than the total; as shares of that sum they are roughly 70% / 30% / 0.2% (derived). WUE could be computed for 458 sites and a non-zero ERF for only 67. The Commission's public dashboard (last updated 25 Sep 2026), read for its 'reporting period 2025' view, shows 773 data centres in 11 countries, total energy consumption of 20.7 TWh, 4.4 GW of installed IT power demand and 8,752,919 m³ of water input, with weighted averages of PUE 1.27, WUE 0.51, REF 0.84 and ERF 0.0236; by size band, very large data centres (90) average a PUE of 1.19 and very small ones (143) 1.52. Its aggregated 2023 and 2024 data were reported as 776 data centres in 18 countries, 6.4 GW, 16.7 TWh and a weighted average PUE of 1.36, with Germany the largest hub [press: DCD]. DG ENER's data-centre page states that a report on the 2025 period is under preparation, that the Commission proposed a common rating scheme on 21 Sept 2026, and that publication of its proposal on minimum performance standards is planned for Q2 2027.

site_or_subject: Metered electricity, water and generator fuel at the 11 EPA-licensed datacentre installations, 2024 and 2025
operator: Amazon Data Services Ireland (9 licences), Microsoft Ireland Operations (DUB14/15), Equinix DB5
record: Each industrial-emissions licensee files an Annual Environmental Report with the EPA; Table 3 gives energy used in GJ by fuel and Table 5 water used in m3. For 2025 the eleven licensed datacentre installations report 14.79 million GJ of electricity (4,109 GWh), 53.6% of the CSO's metered national datacentre total of 7,663 GWh; Amazon's nine licences alone report 3,720 GWh (48.5%). In 2024 the same eleven report 3,585 GWh (51.4% of 6,973 GWh). The largest single installation is Amazon Clonshaugh (P1171-01): 3,673,332 GJ in 2025 (1,020 GWh, 116 MW average). Equinix DB5 is the only installation whose generators burned fuel on a large scale (see ie-equinix-db5-prime-power-gas-2024). At Amazon Grange Castle South (P1170-01), generators burned 1,689 GJ of diesel and HVO in 2025, about one hour of its 460.87 MWth permitted fleet at full rating. Water: 1,133 m3 at P1170-01 in 2025 (down 87%), 399,153 m3 at Equinix DB5 (cooling towers). No AER reports generator run hours.
